title: The Effectiveness and Durability of Pretraining Data Filtering in Protein Language Models
headline: UK AISI research on the effectiveness of pretraining data filtering in protein models
summary: The UK AI Security Institute evaluated the effectiveness and durability of filtering viral proteins from the pretraining data of ESM-2 protein language models. Researchers found that while filtering degrades model performance on viral proteins, this safeguard is not durable against fine-tuning with modest computational resources. The study highlights that performance on removed viral families can be restored for approximately 80 USD of H100 compute time even for large models.
why_it_matters: This research demonstrates that pretraining data filtering is a limited security control for high-risk domains, as it can be easily bypassed by fine-tuning, necessitating more robust assurance strategies for dual-use AI models.

quotes.text: This work establishes pretraining filtering as moderately effective at selectively degrading performance on viral proteins, but not durable against fine-tuning with modest computational resources and access to relevant data.
Although the cost to recover performance increases with model scale, even for the largest models it costs about 80 USD of H100 time.

classification.significance_reason: Provides empirical evidence on the limitations of a common AI safety control (data filtering) for dual-use models, relevant for organisations assessing AI safety and security frameworks.
